{{short description|American chemist}}
'''David M. Leitner''' is an American chemist currently Professor at [[University of Nevada, Reno]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://wolfweb.unr.edu/~dml/DML-group/CV_DML.pdf |title=CV |publisher=unr.edu |accessdate=December 21, 2017 |archive-date=December 22, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222051740/https://wolfweb.unr.edu/~dml/DML-group/CV_DML.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and an Elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.unr.edu/nevada-today/news/2017/two-faculty-members-named-aaas-fellows |title=Two faculty members named AAAS Fellows |date=November 21, 2017 |publisher=unr.edu |accessdate=December 21, 2017}}</ref>

==Education==
He earned his B.S. at [[Cornell University]] in 1985 and then his Ph.D at [[University of Chicago]] in 1989 under [[R. Stephen Berry]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.unr.edu/chemistry/people/david-leitner |title=David M. Leitner |publisher=unr.edu |accessdate=December 21, 2017}}</ref>

==Research==
His interests are energy-molecule relations and his highest paper is ''An extended dynamical hydration shell around proteins'',<ref>Simon Ebbinghaus, Seung Joong Kim, Matthias Heyden, Xin Yu, Udo Heugen, Martin Gruebele, David M Leitner, Martina Havenith. An extended dynamical hydration shell around proteins. 104:52. 20749-20752. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2007</ref> according to Google Scholar.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=hbcekPYAAAAJ&hl=en |title=David Leitner |accessdate=December 21, 2017}}</ref>
